data.description:
Two round-9 **minor** defects from the `ai-agenda` judgement
(`runs/2026-08-13T22-25-26/judgements/ai-agenda.json`). **The area scored 8/8 — no rubric
item punishes either of these.** They are on the list because the agenda builder is the
surface where an organizer makes irreversible scheduling decisions, and both defects hide
information the product already holds.

---

## Part 1 — a conflict badge that names nothing

> **`/agenda-builder` — session tiles in the placement grid and the conflict counter in the
> page header.** The conflict indicator on a scheduled session tile reads only '⚠ Conflict'
> — it never states the reason or the counterpart. When the two Priya Raman sessions were
> overlapped, four tiles in the same 10:00 row carried a conflict marker (two from the new
> overlap, two seeded), and nothing on any tile names the double-booked speaker or the
> session it clashes with, so an organizer cannot tell which tile pairs with which. The
> toolbar's '⚠ 7 conflicts' counter is likewise a bare number with no drill-down shown.

**The product already knows the answer.** Round 4's judge recorded the conflicts panel doing
exactly the right thing: a `LIVE DETECTION — Agenda conflicts · 7` panel naming
*"Grace Isford is double-booked across two sessions."* with both colliding titles and a
`JUMP TO SESSION` action. That panel still exists and it is good.

So this is not a missing feature. It is the same failure the loop keeps finding in different
costumes — **the information exists and the surface the eye lands on does not carry it, and
does not visibly lead to the place that does.** A row with four identical `⚠ Conflict`
badges and a bare `7` in the toolbar gives an organizer no way to pair them up, which is
precisely the moment the detector was built for.

### What to build

1. **The tile badge names its counterpart.** At minimum the double-booked person; better,
   the person and the clashing session. Hover/title text is not enough on its own — the
   organizer is scanning, not pointing.
2. **The counter is a door.** `⚠ 7 conflicts` opens the existing LIVE DETECTION panel. It
   should be visibly actionable rather than a number that happens to be next to a panel.
3. **Pairing is legible.** When several tiles in one row conflict, an organizer must be able
   to tell which two collide — on hover/selection of one tile, mark its counterpart.
4. Do not build a second detector. `src/lib/conflicts.ts` already types this and already
   admits `co_speaker` (MRQ-164). Project what it knows; do not recompute it in the view.
5. **Elements never jump** — a badge that grows to carry a name must not reflow the grid.
   Reserve the space or render into a fixed-width slot.

---

## Part 2 — eleven rooms, four visible

> **`/agenda-builder` — room-column grid.** The agenda builder grid renders one column per
> room and scrolls horizontally with no column condensing or room picker; at a 1280px
> viewport only four of the venue's eleven rooms are visible at once, and a newly created
> room is appended to the far right, so the organizer must scroll sideways to see or verify
> it. The verification that the new 'Overflow Room' had a grid column had to be done through
> the placement-target list rather than the visible grid.

**This is the same defect as MRQ-178** (the `/onboarding` chase grid pushing its newest task
columns off the right edge at 1280px). Same shape, same viewport, same consequence: the
column an organizer most needs — the one they just created — is the one furthest from the
eye, and the judge had to verify it somewhere else.

Read MRQ-178 before designing this, and prefer the same answer in both places so the product
has one idea of a wide grid rather than two. A room picker (or column chooser) with the
newest rooms on by default, a sticky time column, and a visible scroll affordance is the
shape I would expect.

### Acceptance

- At 1280px an organizer can reach and verify a newly created room's column without
  horizontal-scrolling blind, and without leaving the grid to confirm it exists.
- The time (row header) column stays fixed while room columns move.
- No layout jump when columns are toggled or scrolled.

---

## Constraints

- Your **own linked worktree**, created as your first act, then `pwd` and `git branch --show-current` to prove it. Never the primary checkout (it is the Lattice board's home); never `mrq-auto-eval*`.
- **Never `git stash` anywhere in this repo** — the stash stack is shared across every worktree.
- **No migration without the operator.** This needs none.
- **Do not deploy.** An eval round is running and a `.deploy-freeze` marker sits at the primary checkout. Merging is wanted; deploying is not, and is not yours.
- Ship a regression test that fails on `main` and passes on your branch.
- Gate serialized. macOS has no `flock(1)`; wrap it: `python3 -c 'import fcntl,subprocess,sys; f=open("/tmp/marquee-gate.lock","w"); fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX); sys.exit(subprocess.run(["npm","run","pr-gate"]).returncode)'`
- PR: `gh pr create --repo Stage-11-Agentics/marquee --base main`.

> overlap, two seeded), and nothing on any tile names the double-booked speaker or the

> toolbar's '⚠ 7 conflicts' counter is likewise a bare number with no drill-down shown.

**The product already knows the answer.** Round 4's judge recorded the conflicts panel doing
exactly the right thing: a `LIVE DETECTION — Agenda conflicts · 7` panel naming

`JUMP TO SESSION` action. That panel still exists and it is good.

precisely the moment the detector was built for.

> overlapped, four tiles in the same 10:00 row carried a conflict marker (two from the new
> overlap, two seeded), and nothing on any tile names the double-booked speaker or the
> session it clashes with, so an organizer cannot tell which tile pairs with which. The
> toolbar's '⚠ 7 conflicts' counter is likewise a bare number with no drill-down shown.

**The product already knows the answer.** Round 4's judge recorded the conflicts panel doing
exactly the right thing: a `LIVE DETECTION — Agenda conflicts · 7` panel naming
*"Grace Isford is double-booked across two sessions."* with both colliding titles and a
`JUMP TO SESSION` action. That panel still exists and it is good.

So this is not a missing feature. It is the same failure the loop keeps finding in different
costumes — **the information exists and the surface the eye lands on does not carry it, and
does not visibly lead to the place that does.** A row with four identical `⚠ Conflict`
badges and a bare `7` in the toolbar gives an organizer no way to pair them up, which is
precisely the moment the detector was built for.

### What to build

1. **The tile badge names its counterpart.** At minimum the double-booked person; better,
   the person and the clashing session. Hover/title text is not enough on its own — the
   organizer is scanning, not pointing.
2. **The counter is a door.** `⚠ 7 conflicts` opens the existing LIVE DETECTION panel. It
   should be visibly actionable rather than a number that happens to be next to a panel.
3. **Pairing is legible.** When several tiles in one row conflict, an organizer must be able
   to tell which two collide — on hover/selection of one tile, mark its counterpart.
4. Do not build a second detector. `src/lib/conflicts.ts` already types this and already
   admits `co_speaker` (MRQ-164). Project what it knows; do not recompute it in the view.
5. **Elements never jump** — a badge that grows to carry a name must not reflow the grid.
   Reserve the space or render into a fixed-width slot.

---

## Part 2 — eleven rooms, four visible

> **`/agenda-builder` — room-column grid.** The agenda builder grid renders one column per
> room and scrolls horizontally with no column condensing or room picker; at a 1280px
> viewport only four of the venue's eleven rooms are visible at once, and a newly created
> room is appended to the far right, so the organizer must scroll sideways to see or verify
> it. The verification that the new 'Overflow Room' had a grid column had to be done through
> the placement-target list rather than the visible grid.

**This is the same defect as MRQ-178** (the `/onboarding` chase grid pushing its newest task
columns off the right edge at 1280px). Same shape, same viewport, same consequence: the
column an organizer most needs — the one they just created — is the one furthest from the
eye, and the judge had to verify it somewhere else.

Read MRQ-178 before designing this, and prefer the same answer in both places so the product
has one idea of a wide grid rather than two. A room picker (or column chooser) with the
newest rooms on by default, a sticky time column, and a visible scroll affordance is the
shape I would expect.

### Acceptance

- At 1280px an organizer can reach and verify a newly created room's column without
  horizontal-scrolling blind, and without leaving the grid to confirm it exists.
- The time (row header) column stays fixed while room columns move.
- No layout jump when columns are toggled or scrolled.

## Constraints

- **Cut your branch from `github/main`, never local `main`.** The primary checkout's local
  `main` is parked and stale; a local branch pointer in a shared checkout only moves when
  somebody pulls, and nobody does. `git fetch github` then
  `git worktree add ../Marquee-worktrees/<branch> -b <branch> github/main`.
- **Verify freshness with a check that can still fail:**
  `git fetch github && git merge-base --is-ancestor github/main HEAD && echo current || echo 'behind github/main — rebase'`.
  It asks "am I current with main", not "do I have some particular fix" — a check pinned to
  one commit goes vacuous the moment that commit is deep in history and then reassures you
  forever. Behind is normal on a busy night and does not by itself mean broken; but if you
  also see ~22 auth 401 failures, that is expired test-fixture sessions and **rebasing is the
  only cure — re-running never clears it.**
- **Confirm the instrument before you believe a negative browser result.** A dead or stale local
  Worker produces exactly the symptoms of a broken change — blank surface, stuck loader, missing
  styling — and a stale one answers confidently with the wrong program. Before trusting any
  negative reading: `lsof -i :<port>` to confirm something is listening, and
  `curl -s localhost:<port>/health` to confirm the `build_sha` is the commit you think you are
  testing. Ports taken tonight: 8853, 8841, 8871, 8791, 8823. When you report verification
  evidence, name the port, the build_sha, and what you saw.
- **New test titles must start with `CONTRACT` or an `AC-<n>` reference, then a middle dot.**
  `scripts/checks/trace-ac-core.mjs:44` enforces
  `/^((?:AC-\d+(?:\s*[,+]\s*AC-\d+)*)|CONTRACT)\s+·\s+/`, so a bare ticket prefix is rejected:
  `'MRQ-000 · does the thing'` fails, `'CONTRACT · MRQ-000 · does the thing'` passes. Keep the
  ticket reference, just put `CONTRACT` in front of it. This has cost three CI cycles tonight and
  it is invisible until the gate says no.
- **Never `git stash` anywhere in this repo** — the stash stack is shared across every worktree.
- **No migration without the operator.** This needs none.
- **Do not deploy.** An eval round is running and a `.deploy-freeze` marker sits at the primary checkout. Merging is wanted; deploying is not, and is not yours.
- Ship a regression test that fails on `main` and passes on your branch.
- **Gate serialization is a fleet rule, not an option.** Route EVERY `npm run pr-gate` and EVERY full
  `npm test` through `/Users/atin/Projects/Stage11/deployments/Marquee-worktrees/.gate-lock/gate-lock.sh`,
  including one-off "just checking" runs — a lock only serializes its participants, so a single
  unlocked run lands on top of a lock-holder and inflates it. Cheap scoped things (tsc, one test
  file) stay unlocked.
- **A timeout and a red are indistinguishable in an unserialized run.** Check `uptime` before you
  believe a red; load has ranged 14 to 164 tonight and the same branch measured 78s and 276s
